Evidence registry

Ratings use A (convergent standards/reviews and replicated foundations), B (credible convergent evidence with material boundaries), C (limited/direct study or indirect transfer), and D (hypothesis/history only).

ID Evidence and persistent identifier Supports / contradicts Quality Limits
EV-ITTEN-001 CIECAM16, CIE 248:2022, DOI 10.25039/TR.248.2022 appearance depends on viewing conditions A related colors; not a spatial induction model
EV-ITTEN-002 Fairchild & Johnson, iCAM, DOI 10.1109/TIP.2006.884946 spatial/HDR appearance needs more than isolated color coordinates B model performance is image/task dependent
EV-ITTEN-003 Safdar et al., Jzazbz, DOI 10.1364/OE.25.015131 HDR-oriented perceptual modeling B not universal; later refinements exist
EV-ITTEN-004 Luo, Cui & Rigg, CIEDE2000, DOI 10.1002/col.10070 color difference is quantitatively modelable A reference conditions and suprathreshold fit limits
EV-ITTEN-005 Witzel & Gegenfurtner, DOI 10.1037/xhp0000349 categorical perception is conditional, not a complete sensory account B task and language dependent
EV-ITTEN-006 Gibson et al., DOI 10.1073/pnas.1619666114 color naming reflects use and differs across languages B naming is not raw discrimination
EV-ITTEN-007 Lindsey et al., DOI 10.1111/cogs.12907 shared sensory processes coexist with lexical restructuring B two language communities
EV-ITTEN-008 Werner et al., DOI 10.1364/JOSAA.27.000A14 aging reduces chromatic-spatial sensitivity while appearance partly compensates B broadband appearance can remain stable
EV-ITTEN-009 Sinha et al., DOI 10.1016/j.visres.2020.04.012 simultaneous brightness contrast has early contributions B mechanism remains open
EV-ITTEN-010 Blakeslee & McCourt, DOI 10.1016/S0042-6989(99)00186-3 multiscale filtering explains several brightness effects B not all grouping/context phenomena
EV-ITTEN-011 Shevell & Kingdom, DOI 10.1146/annurev.psych.59.103006.093619 chromatic induction is spatial/contextual and mechanism-plural A review predates newest display regimes
EV-ITTEN-012 Lotto & Purves, PMID 11058148 scene statistics/inference can predict color contrast changes B empirical account is contested, not exclusive
EV-ITTEN-013 Faul et al., DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2018.01640 temporal variation suggests separable induction processes C small-sample factor analyses
EV-ITTEN-014 Fairchild, DOI 10.1002/col.20102 classifies appearance effects including contrast and assimilation B taxonomy/review rather than one experiment
EV-ITTEN-015 Hammond et al., DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-78751-2 hue–heat ratings are measurable and intensity dependent C small young sample; ratings, not thermal sensation
EV-ITTEN-016 Levitan et al., DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0101651 crossmodal color associations vary by culture/experience B odor-color, indirect for hue-temperature
EV-ITTEN-017 Itti, Koch & Niebur, DOI 10.1109/34.730558 multiscale feature competition can model bottom-up salience A gaze/task semantics not fully predicted
EV-ITTEN-018 Veale et al., DOI 10.1098/rstb.2016.0113 salience combines feature maps and neural competition A salience is not aesthetic balance
EV-ITTEN-019 Tatler et al., DOI 10.1167/11.5.5 task and scene meaning constrain eye guidance A framework/review; no universal composition score
EV-ITTEN-020 Hathibelagal, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0290782 contradicts global “more saturation fixes CVD” C small sample; some pairs improved
EV-ITTEN-021 Kugler et al., DOI 10.3389/fnhum.2015.00680 CVD impairs peripheral search guidance more than foveal verification B naturalistic but specific red-on-green task
EV-ITTEN-022 Álvaro et al., DOI 10.1038/s41598-022-13877-9 colored filters did not compensate CVD performance B specific filters and tasks
EV-ITTEN-023 WCAG 2.2, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ minimum contrast and no color-only meaning A conformance floor, not performance guarantee
EV-ITTEN-024 ITU-R BT.2390-12, https://www.itu.int/pub/R-REP-BT.2390 HDR pipeline and ambient/viewing conditions matter A broadcast-oriented
EV-ITTEN-025 Land & McCann, DOI 10.1364/JOSA.61.000001 relational computation supports lightness/color constancy A classic model is not complete
